text:
No verified study located that directly compares fixed terminal/interior loss weights against scheduled weights in BERT4Rec while matching training compute and controlling checkpoint-selection bias. The original [BERT4Rec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) studies single-mask versus multiple-mask training and masking proportions; these ablations do not isolate scheduling from terminal-target emphasis. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) identifies the mismatch between random masked-item reconstruction and next-item prediction, but investigates a different training objective rather than the requested weight-schedule control.

The [BERT4Rec replicability study](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.07483) demonstrates that training duration materially affects comparisons. Its implementation uses validation-loss early stopping with 200-epoch patience, while a separate experiment varies training steps; neither establishes the requested scheduling comparison. Validation-based stopping avoids selecting directly on test performance, but does not eliminate optimism from repeatedly selecting on the same validation set.

Recommended experimental controls—not established findings from these papers: compare the schedule against terminal-only, equal-weight, and tuned constant-weight objectives, including a constant matching the schedule’s cumulative terminal/interior weighting. Normalize loss components consistently; match optimizer updates, target counts, and measured GPU time, reporting discrepancies. Keep initialization, sampled histories, masks, evaluation candidates, validation frequency, and checkpoint opportunities paired. Report both a prespecified final checkpoint and validation-selected checkpoints, with equal tuning budgets. Under the fixed RecHarness splits, treat validation improvements as exploratory; reserve the host’s untouched final evaluation for confirmation.
